claims.statement: Promoting to a queen is legal.

hints: A pawn that reaches the far rank must change into another piece.

Move the pawn one square forward to the last rank, then choose the piece.

items.prompt: White to move. The pawn is blocked straight ahead. Capture a piece and promote to a queen.

claims.statement: d7c8q is legal.
The pawn cannot move straight ahead: the square is occupied.

hints: A pawn cannot move forward onto an occupied square. But it can capture diagonally.
A capture on the last rank also promotes the pawn.
Look at the two squares diagonally ahead of the pawn: is an enemy piece standing on one?
items.explain: The pawn cannot push forward because a piece blocks it, but it can capture diagonally onto the last rank, and then it promotes. The capture is legal; the straight push is not.

items.prompt: White to move. Promote the pawn so that it gives checkmate. Which piece should it become?

claims.statement: g7g8n is checkmate.

hints: The pawn may become a queen, a rook, a bishop or a knight. Think about which piece gives check here.
Check the king's escape squares. Which piece attacks the king without giving it a way out?
A queen is the strongest piece, but it is not always the one that gives check from the promotion square.
items.explain: Promoting to a knight gives check from a square the king cannot escape or capture on. A queen would not give check from that square, so the strongest piece is not the right choice here.

items.prompt: White to move. The pawn is about to promote. Choose the promotion that keeps the win.

claims.statement: f7f8r still wins (tablebase).
Promoting to a queen only draws (tablebase).

feedback_by_move.f7f8q: Promoting to a queen leaves the enemy king with no legal move while it is not in check: stalemate, a draw (tablebase: draw).

hints: A queen is usually best, but check what the enemy king can do after the promotion.
Count the squares the enemy king could move to after each promotion. Is the king also attacked?
If the king has no move and is not attacked, the game is drawn at once.
items.explain: A queen would cover every square around the enemy king without attacking it, so the king has no legal move and is not in check: stalemate, a draw. Another promotion keeps the win.
